items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1963-03-29
items.q: But I remember seeing him playing with different bands.

ctx.x: Do you remember when Bunk was playing brass bands?
Bunk Johnson, I remember Bunk Johnson, but I don't remember what brass band he was playing, I really don't remember. But I remember seeing him playing with different bands.
Who played on the street and in the dance bands? Who played in the street and not in the dance bands?

items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-10-14
items.q: That's when Bunk Johnson first came to town.

ctx.x: Well, at the Pelican, when I had the Pelican, when I had the Pelican, the Pelican annex on the bottom, you see. And when the fellas come in at night off the boat and bands come in town, well, that's where they used to go jam all night long.
I won't say dinner there. They must not have had segregation those days. What? That's when Bunk Johnson first came to town. Well, I tell you now, a long time ago,

things were mighty nice around town. That was 1942. I always did go hours ago. I mean, because I know how to care of myself and take care of myself. But I mean, people didn't go all foolish like that. People are foolish, you know. We used to have some boys across the street at my house. The boys would start playing saxophone. My brother and I was playing music and live across the street at my house. We used to go to school together every morning. We used to stand, just carve a school around on the Man Street.…
